description: Collective-intelligence surveys — a named set of ideas someone is asked to choose between, and the response to it: the ideas chosen in priority order plus one new idea that was not in the set. The set is resolved from the survey's name at code generation; L0182 describes no flow and has no interactive player.

example_prompts.prompt: Set up the 'you-can-choose' survey so I can record what I picked.
example_prompts.notes: The canonical starting point — a name and the set resolved from it, with no response yet.

example_prompts.prompt: Create a survey from the team-priorities pool, titled 'Team Priorities', where you may pick at most 5.
example_prompts.notes: `title` and `max-choices` alongside the name. `max-choices` can never exceed the number of ideas.

example_prompts.prompt: Build the survey so each idea keeps the id the service gave it.
example_prompts.notes: Ideas as `{id: "a3" text: "…"}` records. An entry with no id is numbered by position, i0 upward.

example_prompts.prompt: Record that I chose affordable housing, clean air and water, and voting rights, in that order.
example_prompts.notes: `selection` names the ideas chosen and the order is the ranking. An entry is an id in quotes or a position counting from 0 — selection [2 0] — and both work for any set.

example_prompts.prompt: Add my own idea alongside my selection: make public transit free.
example_prompts.notes: `idea` must not repeat one already in the set — that is what makes it new.

example_prompts.prompt: Record just a new idea — I do not want to pick any of the existing ones.
example_prompts.notes: `idea` may stand alone; `selection` comes back empty.
min-choices 2 max-choices 6. The compiler is the only thing enforcing these — there is no player.

example_prompts.prompt: Reorder my selection so the housing idea comes first.
example_prompts.notes: Reordering `selection` IS re-ranking; there is no separate rank step.
